name: Mountain pose
form_cues: Stand with feet hip-width, weight even through both feet.
Lift kneecaps gently and lengthen up through the crown.
Relax shoulders down and breathe slowly.
safety: Safe for nearly everyone; widen stance if balance is poor.
notes: Foundation stance for all standing poses; good for posture awareness.

name: Tree pose
form_cues: Press the lifted foot into the inner calf or thigh, never the knee.
Keep the standing hip stacked over the foot.
Fix your gaze on one still point.
common_mistakes: Resting the foot on the side of the knee
Standing hip jutting out to the side
regressions: Tree pose with toes on the floor (kickstand)
safety: Use a wall for support if balance is unsteady.

name: Warrior I
form_cues: Bend the front knee over the ankle, back foot angled 45 degrees.
Square hips toward the front of the mat.
Reach arms up while dropping shoulders away from ears.
common_mistakes: Front knee drifting past the toes or caving in
Arching the low back to square the hips
regressions: High lunge with back heel lifted
safety: Shorten the stance if hips or knees complain.

name: Warrior II
form_cues: Bend the front knee to track over the middle toes.
Open hips to the long side of the mat.
Reach arms out level and look over the front hand.
common_mistakes: Leaning the torso over the front leg
regressions: Shorter stance with less knee bend
safety: Keep the front knee no further forward than the ankle.

name: Reverse warrior
form_cues: From Warrior II, slide the back hand down the back leg.
Reach the front arm up and back over your ear.
Keep the front knee bent and steady.
common_mistakes: Leaning all your weight on the back hand
safety: Keep the reach gentle if you have low-back pain.

name: Extended side angle
form_cues: From Warrior II, rest the forearm on the front thigh or hand on a block.
Reach the top arm over your ear in one long line.
Roll the top ribs open toward the ceiling.
common_mistakes: Collapsing the chest toward the floor
safety: Use a block under the hand if the floor feels far away.

name: Triangle pose
form_cues: Straighten both legs, front foot pointing forward.
Hinge at the front hip and reach long before tipping down.
Stack shoulders and open the chest to the side.
common_mistakes: Rounding the spine to reach the floor
regressions: Hand on a block or shin
safety: Keep a micro-bend in the front knee if you hyperextend.

name: Revolved triangle
form_cues: Use a shorter stance with hips squared forward.
Lengthen the spine first, then twist from the ribs.
Place the bottom hand on a block if needed.
common_mistakes: Twisting from the neck instead of the torso
Losing balance by keeping feet on one line
safety: Avoid deep twists if pregnant or with disc issues.

name: Chair pose
form_cues: Sit hips back as if onto a chair, weight in the heels.
Keep knees behind the toes.
Reach arms up and draw the belly in.
common_mistakes: Letting knees drift far past the toes
regressions: Wall sit with hands on thighs
safety: Keep the bend shallower if knees hurt.

name: Revolved chair
form_cues: From Chair pose, bring palms together at the chest.
Hook the elbow outside the opposite knee.
Keep knees level and twist from the upper back.
common_mistakes: One knee sliding forward past the other
Rounding the back instead of lengthening
safety: Skip deep twists if pregnant or with a disc injury.

name: Standing forward fold
form_cues: Hinge from the hips with a long spine.
Bend knees as much as you need.
Let the head and neck hang heavy.
common_mistakes: Locking the knees and rounding hard
safety: Rise slowly to avoid dizziness; bend knees if you have back pain.

name: Wide-legged forward fold
form_cues: Step feet wide, toes slightly in.
Hinge from the hips with hands on the floor or blocks.
Lengthen the crown toward the floor.
common_mistakes: Rounding only from the upper back
safety: Rise slowly with a flat back to avoid dizziness.

name: Pyramid pose
form_cues: Step one foot back about a leg's length, hips square.
Fold over the front leg with a long spine.
Keep the front knee soft, not locked.
common_mistakes: Rounding to get the head lower
safety: Shorten the stance if hamstrings feel sharp, not stretched.

name: Eagle pose
form_cues: Sit into a slight squat, wrap one thigh over the other.
Cross arms and lift elbows to shoulder height.
Squeeze everything toward the midline.
common_mistakes: Shoulders hunched up to the ears
regressions: Toes of the top leg on the floor
safety: Skip the leg wrap if you have knee pain.

name: Dancer pose
form_cues: Hold the inside of one foot behind you.
Kick the foot into the hand as you tip forward.
Reach the free arm forward for balance.
common_mistakes: Letting the lifted knee splay out wide
regressions: Standing quad stretch at a wall
safety: Use a wall or strap; ease off with low-back pain.

name: Half moon pose
form_cues: Balance on one leg with the bottom hand on a block.
Lift the top leg to hip height, foot flexed.
Stack hips and open the chest to the side.
regressions: Half moon with back to a wall
safety: Practise near a wall until balance is steady.

name: Goddess pose
form_cues: Take a wide stance, toes turned out.
Bend knees over the toes and sink hips.
Keep the spine tall and arms in cactus.
safety: Keep knees in line with toes to protect them.

name: Extended hand-to-big-toe pose
form_cues: Hook the big toe with two fingers or use a strap.
Stand tall on a firm standing leg.
Extend the lifted leg forward, then open it to the side.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back to straighten the leg
Hiking the hip of the lifted leg
safety: Use a strap or bend the knee to avoid straining the hamstring.

name: Garland pose
form_cues: Squat deep with feet a little wider than hips.
Press elbows into the inner knees, palms together.
Lift the chest and keep heels down if you can.
common_mistakes: Heels lifting and weight rolling forward
regressions: Block under the hips or rolled mat under heels
safety: Sit on a block if knees are sensitive.

name: High lunge
form_cues: Stay on the ball of the back foot, back leg strong.
Bend the front knee to about 90 degrees.
Square the hips and reach arms up.
safety: Shorten the stance for knee comfort.

name: Legs up the wall
form_cues: Sit sideways to a wall and swing legs up.
Rest your back and head on the floor.
Let arms fall open and breathe slowly.
common_mistakes: Hips too far from the wall with straining hamstrings
safety: Come down if your feet go numb; check with a doctor if you have glaucoma.

name: Downward dog
form_cues: Press hands wide and lift hips up and back.
Bend knees to keep the spine long.
Let heels sink toward the floor.
common_mistakes: Shoulders crunched up to the ears
safety: Rest in child's pose if wrists or shoulders hurt.

name: Child's pose
form_cues: Sit hips toward the heels with knees wide or together.
Reach arms forward or rest them by your sides.
Breathe into the back of the ribs.
common_mistakes: Forcing hips down when knees hurt
safety: Place a cushion behind the knees if knee flexion hurts.

name: Cat-cow
form_cues: Start on hands and knees, wrists under shoulders.
Inhale, drop the belly and lift chest.
Exhale, round the spine and tuck the chin.
common_mistakes: Rushing instead of matching the breath
safety: Keep the range pain-free; pad the knees if needed.
notes: Moving flow, counted in breath cycles rather than held.

name: Low lunge
form_cues: Lower the back knee to the mat, front knee over ankle.
Sink hips forward and lift the chest.
Reach arms overhead without arching the low back.
common_mistakes: Front knee shooting past the toes
safety: Pad the back knee with a folded mat.

name: Four-limbed staff pose
form_cues: From plank, shift forward onto the toes.
Lower with elbows hugging the ribs.
Stop when upper arms are parallel to the floor.
safety: Lower with control and stop above shoulder height to protect shoulders.

name: Upward-facing dog
form_cues: Press through straight arms, thighs lifted off the mat.
Roll shoulders back and open the chest.
Press the tops of the feet down.
safety: Use cobra instead with low-back or wrist pain.

name: Cobra pose
form_cues: Lie face down, hands under the shoulders.
Lift the chest using the back, little weight in the hands.
Keep elbows bent and close to the ribs.
common_mistakes: Pushing to straight arms and crunching the low back
safety: Keep the lift low if you feel low-back pinching.

name: Sphinx pose
form_cues: Lie on your belly with elbows under the shoulders.
Press forearms down and lift the chest.
Relax glutes and let the spine lengthen.
regressions: Lie flat with a pillow under the chest
safety: Lower down if you feel pinching in the lower back.

name: Locust pose
form_cues: Lie face down, arms by your sides.
Lift chest, arms and legs together.
Look slightly down to keep the neck long.
safety: Keep the lift modest with low-back issues.

name: Bow pose
form_cues: Lie face down and hold the outside of the ankles.
Kick feet into hands to lift chest and thighs.
Keep knees about hip-width.
safety: Avoid if pregnant or with acute back pain.

name: Camel pose
form_cues: Kneel with hips over knees, hands on the low back.
Lift the chest up before leaning back.
Reach for the heels only if the hips stay forward.
common_mistakes: Hips drifting back behind the knees
safety: Come up slowly; skip with neck or low-back injuries.

name: Bridge pose
form_cues: Lie on your back, feet hip-width near the hips.
Press feet down and lift hips high.
Roll shoulders under and interlace hands below you.
safety: Keep the neck still while the hips are up.
notes: Yoga version focuses on chest opening; see Glute bridge for strength reps.

name: Wheel pose
form_cues: Place hands by the ears, fingers toward the shoulders.
Press up onto the crown, then straighten arms.
Keep feet and knees parallel.
regressions: Wheel with blocks at a wall
safety: Warm up well first; avoid with shoulder, wrist or back injuries.

name: Fish pose
form_cues: Lie on your back with hands under the hips.
Press forearms down to lift the chest.
Rest the crown lightly or keep the head lifted.
common_mistakes: Putting body weight into the head
safety: Keep weight off the head if you have neck issues.

name: Pigeon pose
form_cues: Bring one shin forward across the mat.
Extend the back leg straight behind you.
Keep hips level, then fold forward slowly.
common_mistakes: Hips tipping onto the front-leg side
safety: Switch to the supine figure-four if the front knee hurts.

name: Seated forward fold
form_cues: Sit tall with legs straight, feet flexed.
Hinge forward from the hips, leading with the chest.
Bend knees if the back starts rounding.
common_mistakes: Rounding hard to touch the toes
safety: Bend the knees if you feel nerve tingling.

name: Head-to-knee pose
form_cues: Extend one leg, other foot against the inner thigh.
Turn the chest over the straight leg.
Fold from the hips with a long spine.
common_mistakes: Rounding from the upper back only
Forcing the head to the knee
safety: Pad under the bent knee if it lifts high.

name: Bound angle pose
form_cues: Sit with soles of the feet together.
Hold the feet and sit tall.
Let knees relax down, no pushing.
common_mistakes: Pressing knees down with the hands
safety: Support the knees with blocks if groin feels strained.

name: Reclined bound angle
form_cues: Lie back with soles of the feet together.
Let knees fall open, supported if needed.
Rest arms by your sides and breathe slowly.
safety: Support the knees if you feel groin or knee strain.

name: Boat pose
form_cues: Balance just behind the sit bones.
Lift shins parallel to the floor, chest proud.
Reach arms forward alongside the knees.
regressions: Half boat with hands behind the thighs
safety: Keep knees bent if the low back aches.

name: Seated spinal twist
form_cues: Cross one foot outside the opposite knee.
Lengthen up on the inhale.
Twist on the exhale, hugging the knee.
progressions: Bound half lord of the fishes
safety: Twist gently; avoid deep twists if pregnant or with a disc injury.

name: Supine spinal twist
form_cues: Lie on your back and draw one knee across the body.
Open the opposite arm out wide.
Let shoulders stay heavy on the mat.
common_mistakes: Lifting the shoulder to get the knee down
progressions: Twist with the top leg extended
safety: Keep it gentle with back injuries.

name: Happy baby
form_cues: Lie on your back and hold the outer feet.
Stack ankles over knees.
Draw knees toward the armpits, tailbone heavy.
regressions: Hold the shins or use a strap
safety: Avoid pressure on the belly late in pregnancy.

name: Corpse pose
form_cues: Lie on your back with legs and arms relaxed apart.
Close your eyes and let the breath be natural.
Release tension from face, jaw and shoulders.
safety: Bend the knees or use a pillow if the low back aches.

name: Supported shoulder stand
form_cues: Swing legs over, hands supporting the back.
Walk elbows in toward each other.
Stack hips over shoulders, weight on shoulders not neck.
safety: Avoid with neck injury, high blood pressure or glaucoma; fold blankets under the shoulders.

name: Plough pose
form_cues: From shoulder stand, lower the toes behind the head.
Keep hips stacked over the shoulders.
Keep the neck still and the throat soft.
regressions: Feet on a chair behind you
safety: Avoid with neck injury, glaucoma or high blood pressure.

name: Supported headstand
form_cues: Interlace fingers and cradle the back of the head.
Press forearms down to lift weight off the head.
Walk feet in, then lift legs slowly with control.
safety: Learn with a teacher; avoid with neck injury, high blood pressure or glaucoma.

name: Crow pose
form_cues: Plant hands shoulder-width and bend elbows back.
Rest knees high on the backs of the upper arms.
Shift forward and lift one foot, then the other.
common_mistakes: Looking straight down and tipping over
safety: Put a pillow in front of your face while learning; skip with wrist pain.

name: Side crow
form_cues: Squat and twist so both knees face one side.
Plant hands, stack the outer thigh on one arm.
Lean forward and float the feet.
safety: Skip with wrist injuries; use a cushion in front.

name: Dolphin pose
form_cues: Start on forearms, elbows shoulder-width.
Lift hips up and back into an inverted V.
Press forearms down and push away from the floor.
safety: Use a strap above the elbows if they splay.

name: Lizard pose
form_cues: From low lunge, place both hands inside the front foot.
Lower the back knee or keep it lifted.
Drop to forearms or blocks if hips allow.
progressions: Lizard with a back-leg quad stretch
safety: Pad the back knee; ease off with groin pain.

name: Cow face pose
form_cues: Stack one knee over the other, feet by the hips.
Reach one arm up and one behind, clasp fingers.
Sit evenly on both sit bones.
common_mistakes: One hip lifting off the floor
Arching the back to reach hands
safety: Use a strap; avoid if knee or shoulder pain.

name: Puppy pose
form_cues: Start on hands and knees, walk hands forward.
Keep hips above the knees.
Melt the chest toward the mat, forehead down.
common_mistakes: Hips sinking back toward the heels
safety: Ease off with shoulder impingement.

name: Hero pose
form_cues: Kneel with knees together and feet just wider than hips.
Sit between the feet, on a block if needed.
Lengthen the spine with hands on thighs.
common_mistakes: Feet splaying out and twisting the knees
safety: Use a block and stop with any knee pain.

name: Supported bridge
form_cues: Lift hips and slide a block under the sacrum.
Rest your weight onto the block.
Relax arms beside you and breathe.
common_mistakes: Block under the low back instead of the sacrum
safety: Remove the block and lower slowly if the back feels pinched.

name: Sun salutation A
form_cues: Link one movement to each breath.
Move through mountain, fold, plank, chaturanga, cobra, down dog.
Step or jump forward and rise back to standing.
safety: Drop knees in plank and skip chaturanga if shoulders are weak.

name: Sun salutation B
form_cues: Begin and end each round in chair pose.
Add Warrior I on each side between vinyasas.
Keep each move on a single breath.
safety: Modify chaturanga to knees-down if form fades.
notes: More heating than A; 3–5 rounds is typical.

name: Pilates hundred
form_cues: Curl head and shoulders up, legs in tabletop or extended.
Pump straight arms by your sides.
Inhale for 5 pumps, exhale for 5.
safety: Keep the head down if the neck strains.

name: Pilates roll-up
form_cues: Lie long with arms overhead.
Curl up one vertebra at a time and reach for the toes.
Roll down slowly with control.
safety: Bend knees or use a strap with low-back issues.

name: Pilates rollover
form_cues: Lift straight legs over the head, toes toward the floor.
Flex the feet and roll down one bone at a time.
Lower legs only as far as the back stays down.
common_mistakes: Using momentum to throw legs over
safety: Avoid with neck problems or osteoporosis.

name: Single-leg circles
form_cues: Lie on your back, one leg up to the ceiling.
Draw circles from the hip, keeping pelvis still.
Keep circles small enough for a stable trunk.
safety: Keep circles small if the hip clicks or hurts.

name: Rolling like a ball
form_cues: Hug the shins and balance behind the sit bones.
Keep a tight C-curve and roll back to the shoulder blades.
Roll up and balance without feet touching.
safety: Avoid with osteoporosis or spine injuries; never roll onto the neck.

name: Single-leg stretch
form_cues: Curl head and shoulders up, one knee in.
Extend the other leg long and low.
Switch legs smoothly without rocking.
common_mistakes: Low back arching off the mat
Pulling on the knee with the neck
safety: Keep the extended leg higher to protect the low back.

name: Double-leg stretch
form_cues: Hug both knees in with head curled up.
Reach arms back and legs forward together.
Circle arms round and hug back in.
safety: Keep legs higher if the low back arches.

name: Pilates scissors
form_cues: Curl up with both legs straight.
Hold one leg and pulse it toward you twice.
Switch legs in a scissor motion.
safety: Keep the head down if the neck tires.

name: Double straight-leg stretch
form_cues: Hands behind the head, legs straight up.
Lower legs only as far as the back stays down.
Exhale and lift legs back up.
common_mistakes: Low back arching off the mat
safety: Shorten the range at the first sign of back arching.

name: Criss-cross
form_cues: Hands behind the head, curl up.
Rotate one armpit toward the opposite knee.
Extend the other leg long and switch.
common_mistakes: Pulling the elbow instead of rotating ribs
safety: Keep the neck long and relaxed.

name: Spine stretch forward
form_cues: Sit tall, legs straight and wider than hips.
Exhale and peel the spine forward like a C.
Restack one vertebra at a time.
safety: Sit on a raised surface if hamstrings are tight.

name: Open-leg rocker
form_cues: Balance holding ankles, legs straight in a V.
Roll back to the shoulder blades.
Roll up to balance with legs still open.
common_mistakes: Collapsing the chest on the way up
safety: Avoid with spinal injuries or osteoporosis.

name: Corkscrew
form_cues: Lie on your back, legs together straight up.
Circle both legs to one side, down and around.
Keep shoulders heavy on the mat.
safety: Keep circles small with low-back pain.

name: Pilates saw
form_cues: Sit tall, legs wide, arms out.
Twist toward one leg, then reach the little finger past the little toe.
Restack and return to center.
safety: Keep the twist gentle with back issues.

name: Pilates swan
form_cues: Lie face down, hands by the shoulders.
Lift the chest by lengthening up through the crown.
Lower with control.
safety: Keep the lift small with low-back pain.

name: Single-leg kick
form_cues: Lie prone, propped on forearms, belly lifted.
Kick one heel to the glute twice.
Switch legs, keeping hips on the mat.
safety: Lie flatter with low-back pain.

name: Pilates shoulder bridge
form_cues: Lift into a bridge with hands supporting or on the floor.
Extend one leg up to the ceiling.
Lower the leg to knee height and lift, hips level.
common_mistakes: Hips dropping on the working side
safety: Keep the range small if hamstrings cramp.

name: Spine twist
form_cues: Sit tall, legs together, arms out.
Twist from the waist, pulsing twice.
Return to center growing taller.
safety: Twist gently with back issues.

name: Side kick
form_cues: Lie on your side, legs slightly forward.
Kick the top leg forward twice, then sweep back.
Keep the torso still.
safety: Prop the head on the hand to keep the neck easy.

name: Teaser
form_cues: Lift legs and torso into a V, arms parallel to legs.
Balance on the sit bones with a lifted chest.
Roll down slowly and repeat.
safety: Avoid with back injury; build up with single-leg versions.

name: Pilates swimming
form_cues: Lie face down, reach arms and legs long.
Lift opposite arm and leg in quick flutters.
Keep the gaze down and the neck long.
safety: Keep the lift small with low-back pain.

name: Leg pull front
form_cues: Start in a straight-arm plank.
Lift one leg and pulse the foot.
Lower and switch without moving the hips.
safety: Drop to a plank hold if the wrists hurt.

name: Leg pull back
form_cues: Sit with hands behind, lift into reverse plank.
Kick one leg up, then lower with control.
Keep hips high throughout.
safety: Point fingers toward the feet; skip with shoulder pain.

name: Pilates ring thigh squeeze
form_cues: Place the ring between the knees or ankles.
Squeeze slowly for 2 seconds.
Release with control without letting it drop.
safety: Keep pressure moderate after groin injuries.

name: Pilates ring chest press
form_cues: Hold the ring at chest height, palms on the pads.
Squeeze the ring with soft elbows.
Keep shoulders down away from ears.
safety: Use light pressure with shoulder pain.

name: Side-lying ring leg press
form_cues: Lie on your side with the ring between the ankles.
Press the top leg down into the ring.
Lift back up against the outside pad.
safety: Prop the head to keep the neck easy.

name: Pilates ring bridge
form_cues: Ring between the knees, feet hip-width.
Roll up into a bridge one bone at a time.
Squeeze the ring at the top, then roll down.
common_mistakes: Arching the low back at the top
safety: Keep the weight off the neck.

name: Reformer footwork
form_cues: Lie on the carriage with feet on the footbar.
Press out to straight legs without locking.
Return with control, resisting the springs.
safety: Use lighter springs and avoid locking knees.
notes: Positions: toes, arches, heels, wide V; 2–4 springs typical.

name: Long stretch
form_cues: Hold the footbar in a plank, heels on the headrest.
Push the carriage back from the shoulders.
Pull it in keeping a straight line.
safety: Use 1–2 springs; stop with wrist or shoulder pain.

name: Elephant
form_cues: Stand on the carriage, hands on the footbar, hips high.
Push the carriage back with the legs.
Draw it in using the abs.
safety: Keep the range short if hamstrings are tight.

name: Reformer rowing
form_cues: Sit tall on the carriage holding the straps.
Pull the straps with elbows bent, rolling back.
Sit up and circle arms round.
safety: Use light springs; keep the back long.

name: Knee stretches
form_cues: Kneel on the carriage, hands on the footbar.
Push the carriage back with a round back.
Draw it in with the abs.
safety: Pad knees; use 1–2 springs.

name: Short spine massage
form_cues: Feet in straps, legs out.
Lift legs over, rolling the spine up.
Roll down slowly one bone at a time.
safety: Avoid with neck issues or osteoporosis.

name: Feet in straps
form_cues: Lie on the carriage, feet in straps.
Move through frogs, circles and openings.
Keep the pelvis steady.
safety: Use light springs and keep range pain-free.

name: Pulling straps
form_cues: Lie prone on the long box, holding the straps.
Pull arms down by your sides, lifting the chest.
Return slowly with control.
safety: Use a light spring and lift the chest only slightly.

name: Mermaid
form_cues: Sit sideways on the carriage, hand on the footbar.
Push the carriage out as you side-bend.
Return and reach the other way.
safety: Keep it gentle with shoulder pain.
